quandoUsar: Comparing the shape of several distributions at once: daily temperatures by month, response times by region.
When the question is about shift and spread: where each group's median is and how wide the middle half is.
Showing how distributions change between two datasets: with the same `id`s, each curve transforms into the new one.
quandoEvitar: Use `bar-chart` when each group has a single value, not a collection of observations.
Use `line-chart` or `streamgraph` when the horizontal axis is time and you want to see evolution, not distribution.
With few observations per group, the smoothed curve suggests a shape the data doesn't support; prefer showing the values.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, pick the previous or next ridge and raise it.
Move the reading cursor along the values, one axis step at a time.
Go to the first or last ridge.
Releases the raised ridge and hides the tooltip.

acessibilidade: The `<figure>` carries the `label`; the chart area is a focusable group with `aria-roledescription="ridgeline chart"` and the keyboard instructions in its name, in English.
An `aria-live="polite"` region reads the active series (median, middle half, range, and count) and, with the cursor, the fraction of values up to that point.
A hidden table lists the median, quartiles, minimum, maximum, and count of each series, so screen readers don't depend on the drawing.
movimento: On entering the viewport, the ridges grow from the baseline in a wave, from top to bottom; when the data changes, each curve and the axis transform on a spring to the new shape.
The ridge under the pointer rises 6 px on a copy drawn on top, with the band between the quartiles highlighted, while the others fade; the tooltip follows the pointer on a spring.
With “reduced motion” on, shapes are painted directly in the final state and the tooltip follows the pointer without a spring.
responsivo: The width follows the container and the height comes from the content: `rowHeight` per series plus the overlap and axis space; there is no total height prop.
Below 420 px of width the name column shrinks from 52 to 36 px, with ellipses, and the axis shows fewer ticks (about one every 72 px).
desempenho: Density is computed in the browser (96 samples per series, each against all observations) and `series` is serialized on every render, including when moving the pointer; with many thousands of values, downsample first.
notasIA: Pass raw observations in `values`, not ready-made densities: the component estimates the curve with Silverman's rule per series, or with `bandwidth` in value units.
Use a stable `id` per series so the curves transform when the data is swapped, and fix `domain` when two datasets need the same axis.
`active` with `onActiveChange` controls the raised ridge; `tint` (on by default) colors each ridge by its median and shows the scale below the chart.
